chapter: Des Moines childhood and first bands
title: Getting his first alto and learning from records instead of lessons
summary: His mother gave him an alto saxophone for Christmas and sent him to teacher Charles Bushman, whose first lesson was the chromatic scale. He spent the lesson money on movies and learned by copying Coleman Hawkins and others from records.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: Yeah, I just liked the looks of it. I told my mother I wanted a saxophone. She said, 'well, I've spent money with you for piano lessons and you gave it up. Do you think you'll stick with this?' I said, 'Mama, get me a saxophone and I'll learn to play it.' And I wanted a C melody saxophone because, see, you didn't have to transpose, in those days. You could play from the piano sheet. So anyway, we were strong believers in Christmas and Santa Claus, you know. This Christmas, sure enough when I woke up Christmas morning, under the Christmas tree was a brand new York (PHONETIC) alto saxophone. And there was a note that said, 'Santa Claus didn't have any more C melodies but he said the alto is going to be very popular so this is the one you should learn.' All right, great. I took the instrument and now -- I was sort of mechanically inclined in those days and the first thing I did was take all the keys off to see how it was put together. And then my mother she was flabbergasted, you know. She had to put it all in a bag, keys and all, and take it back down to the store and have it reassembled. When she brought it back she said, 'Now, you can't touch it until I get you a teacher.' So she found me a teacher whose name was Charles Bushman, lived on 9th Street in Des Moines. And she took me to him; 50 cents a lesson. The first lesson, he taught me the

chromatic scale. Well, that's all I needed. I went home and we had records all of these years and I started fooling around playing what those little things I had in my ear. And I started copying Coleman Hawkins who was the first saxophone player that I remember hearing. And he was recording with Fletcher Henderson's band in 1923. I remember when they picked him up and brought him -- Fletcher Henderson and Mamie Smith brought him out of St. Joseph, Missouri.

I started to learn these things from the record. When my mother gave me the 50 cents every week to take the lesson, I would go deposit myself horn in the drug store and go to the movies and then come home and practice with the records. She would say, "is that your lesson?" And I would say, "fine", yes, that's my lesson." This is actually the way I learned how to play. I didn't know scales or chords about.
Did you read any music at this time?
